summary: Split once while retaining whether a separator was found.
documentation: partition splits at the first occurrence of a nonempty separator and returns before, separator and after. When absent, the original text is first and the final two components are empty strings.
caution: An empty separator raises ValueError. Later occurrences stay in the final component; this is not the same as splitting everywhere.
scenarios: Parse a configuration assignment while keeping equals signs in its value.
Separate an internal record prefix from its remainder.
Inspect a header field whose value can contain the separator.
title: Parse one configuration assignment
problem: Input is a string. Return the three partition components as a list using the first = separator. Keep later equals signs in the last component and preserve whitespace.
goal: Use str.partition() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
hint: Partition once, then turn the tuple into a list.
